cohort: The study involved 221 male babies (73 cases of hypospadias and 148 controls) born at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2016.
finding: Hypospadias was more frequent in boys born by Caesarean section, those with low birth weight, and those small for gestational age; maternal alcohol use, smoking, herbal use, medical history, multiple pregnancies, and maternal congenital abnormalities were associated with an increased risk of hypospadias.
mod_finding: Hypospadias was more frequent in boys born by Caesarean Section.
birth_weight: The study included boys with hypospadias and those without, noting that hypospadias was more frequent in boys with low birth weight.
